special_checks.check: (a) s6 exam_note on Birbal and Din-i-Ilahi
special_checks.detail: The only Din-i-Ilahi / Birbal content in the chapter is the s6 exam_note box 'দীন-ই-ইলাহি প্রসঙ্গে'. It (i) gives the standard exam answer (founder: Akbar) explicitly as exam guidance, (ii) states that what the chapter actually teaches from the sources is Akbar's murid (disciple) circle and his light/sun-centred eclectic worship, and (iii) expressly refuses to claim 'Birbal was the first member', saying that popular fact is absent from the chapter's two NCERT sources and is therefore not claimed. The two claims attached to the note, c25 (murid) and c48 (eclectic worship focused on light and the sun), were both verified verbatim against lehs205 in the page_checks below. The name 'Birbal' occurs nowhere in gess104.txt or lehs205.txt (full-text search), and elsewhere in the chapter Birbal appears only as a distractor in q07. The chapter never presents the name 'Din-i-Ilahi' itself as a sourced fact — only as the label used in exam questions.

Increasingly, he moved away from the orthodox Islamic ways of understanding religions towards a self-conceived eclectic form of divine worship focused on light and the sun.

special_checks.check: (c2) 'Taught with caveats' — English factory at Surat (WBCS-2019-Q67, mapped to s8)
special_checks.verdict: SUPPORTED ONLY BY CONTEXT + EXAM FRAMING — caveat is necessary and is honestly disclosed
special_checks.detail: Section s8 teaches Thomas Roe's embassy to Jahangir's court from lehs205, and s7 teaches Jahanara's revenues from the port city of Surat, also from lehs205. The s8 prose sentence about the Surat factory is explicitly framed as exam guidance ('পরীক্ষায় ইংরেজদের সুরাটে প্রথম কারখানার অনুমতিও জাহাঙ্গিরের নামেই আসে'). The deciding fact itself — Jahangir's farman permitting the first English factory at Surat (1613) — appears in NEITHER gess104 nor lehs205 (verified by full-text search: Surat occurs in lehs205 only in the Jahanara passage; no factory or farman is mentioned). So the chapter points a student to the official answer (Jahangir) through context and a transparent exam note, not through a sourced statement of the fact. pyq_map's note and REPORT.md disclose exactly this. Judgement: the 'taught with caveats' mark is fair, but this is the weaker of the two caveats — the underlying fact remains uncorroborated by the allowed sources.
